entries.value: Analysts demonstrate mappings with examples and recognize the intended result within a synthesized candidate pool (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "In general, rather than having to construct a visualization, data analysts demonstrate the task using examples and then select the desired visualization from a candidate pool, which shifts from the challenges of expression to the ease of recognition." (p. 2)

entries.value: Prior synthesis interactions could require users to read synthesized programs to disambiguate results (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "Third, instead of asking Amelia to read synthesized programs to disambiguate synthesis results, Falx provides an exploration interface that allows Amelia to explore and examine results in the visualization space." (p. 4)

entries.value: Falx users inspect candidate visualizations from coarse form through axes, differences, and exact values before choosing (PDF pp. 11-12).
quotes: "We discovered from the interview that many participants shared the following similar 4-step process to select the desired visualization from synthesized visualizations by investigating visualization from coarse to fine:" (p. 11)
"After these steps, participants were confident about the result." (p. 12)

entries.value: In the conventional R workflow, analysts fine-tuned visualization parameters in ggplot2 code (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "She also fine-tunes some parameters in ggplot2 to improve visualization aesthetics (e.g., modify titles of the axes and change line chart to a step chart), which generates the visualization that matches her design in Figure 3." (p. 3)

entries.value: Analysts can revise the selected design through graphical controls with immediate feedback, while retaining optional direct access to the generated program (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "Any changes made during the editing process are directly reflected on the center view panel (Figure 5- 2○) to provide immediate feedback." (p. 4)
"If Amelia wants to further customize the visualization (e.g., change color scheme, adjust bar spacing), she can directly edit the underlying Vega-Lite program." (p. 4)

rq3_entries.value: Falx infers visualization and data-transformation programs, generates candidate visualizations, and groups and ranks them for exploration (PDF pp. 6, 8).
quotes: "Given an input data and an example visualization (in the form of a set of geometric objects), Falx synthesizes pairs of candidate data transformation and visualization programs such that the resulting visualization contains all geometric objects in the visualization example." (p. 6)
"Finally, Falx groups and ranks the visualizations based on the complexity of the programs (numbers of expressions)." (p. 8)

rq3_entries.value: The analyst constructs and revises examples, then judges candidate form, invariants, differences, and exact values before selecting and customizing a result (PDF pp. 11-12).
quotes: "Data analysts initiate interactions with Falx by creating examples." (p. 11)

"In sum, Falx’s exploration panel allowed users to directly inspect solutions in the visualization space following a coarse-to-fine process, which helped them to disambiguate solutions and trust the chosen results." (p. 12)

The claim is bounded to effective adoption and occasional speed gains, matching the one significant completion-rate advantage, two significant time advantages, and reported null comparisons (PDF pp. 9-10).
quotes: "We observed a statistically significant difference in the completion rate in the car sales visualization (𝑝< 0.05); ... others were not significant." (p. 9)

"While Falx participants were also generally faster in the other two tasks, there was no significant difference for the movie ... industry celebrity visualization ... or the disaster impact visualization ..." (pp. 9-10)
"Modern visualization tools aim to allow data analysts to easily create exploratory visualizations." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: both — immediate visualization authoring is operational, while learning to create visualizations is an author-stated use not measured in the study (PDF pp. 13-14).
quotes: "Our goal was to create a system that does not require users to manually specify the visualization or worry about data transformations, thereby improving user efficiency and reducing the learning burden on novice analysts." (p. 13)
"Falx can fill in this gap by helping data analysts to learn to create visualizations." (p. 14)

paper_code_entries.value: mixed_or_transitioning — the Falx group ranged from zero prior authoring experience to experienced visualization-tool users (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "For the Falx study group, there were 6 participants experienced with some visualization tools (created >10 visualizations), 8 with moderate experience with visualization tools (created 1-10 visualizations), and 2 participants with zero experience in creating visualizations in the past." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: execution_or_skill_gap — users could have an intended transformation yet lack the vocabulary or implementation skill to realize it (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "R14 mentioned that “I had an idea of what I needed to do, but I wasn’t able to search the right things on Google to arrive at a useful code snippet for it.”" (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: process — task-completion time and authoring strategies were measured (PDF pp. 9, 11).
quotes: "Figure 12: Violin plot showing the amount of time participants spent on each task for both Falx and R study groups." (p. 9)
"We conducted an inductive content analysis on the interviewer’s notes about Falx experience similar to that in Section 4.4." (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — correctness required the submitted visualization’s semantics to match the example solution (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Finally, we asked participants that they do not need to optimize the design — a task was considered correctly solved as long as the semantics of the visualization created by the participant matched the example solution regardless of the process and details." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the interface organizes authoring into example construction, candidate exploration, and post-processing (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "Figure 5: Falx interface has three panels: (1) Data analysts import data and create examples in the input panel. (2) Analysts explore and examine synthesized visualizations in the exploration panel. (3) Analysts edit visualization details in the post processing panel." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — synthesized transformations and visualizations respond to the user’s current geometric examples (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Given an input data and an example visualization (in the form of a set of geometric objects), Falx synthesizes pairs of candidate data transformation and visualization programs such that the resulting visualization contains all geometric objects in the visualization example." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: generative_non_llm — program synthesis generates transformation and visualization programs from examples (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Given an input data and an example visualization (in the form of a set of geometric objects), Falx synthesizes pairs of candidate data transformation and visualization programs such that the resulting visualization contains all geometric objects in the visualization example." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the meaning-producing path is example-driven program synthesis rather than a language or foundation model (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "In recent years, many program synthesis algorithms have been developed to automate challenging or repetitive tasks for end users by automatically generating programs from high-level specifications (e.g., demonstrations, input-output examples, natural language descriptions)." (p. 5)

limitations: "However, several participants also mentioned Falx may not fit well to their current workflow when they need “very high standard visualizations” (F1) that requires extensive customization." (PDF p. 12)

"Another limitation of the current version of Falx is the lack of “deep integration with other tools” (F1), e.g., database for handling big datasets and data cleaning tools for “handling null / dirty data” (F4)." (PDF p. 12)
"Falx currently does not support directly visualizing dirty or non-relational data." (PDF p. 13)
boundary_conditions: "Each participant was asked to complete four visualization tasks, where the Falx study group completed the task using Falx and the baseline group used R to complete the task." (PDF p. 8)
"The total session was less than 2 hours for all participants." (PDF p. 9)
"Falx, in comparison, supports standard visualization designs but automates data transformation." (PDF p. 13)
"Falx currently focuses on inexperienced data analysts, but it could also potentially benefit experienced data analysts by bootstrapping complex data analysis tasks." (PDF p. 14)
cards.claim: Falx users could adopt the tool for otherwise unsolved visualization tasks and were faster in some cases
